punchline: A horse that mostly lost beat the champion after his trainer taught him to leave at the sound of a bell.
thirty_sec: Seabiscuit was a small, knobby-kneed horse that mostly lost. Charles Howard bought him for $8,000 and gave him to trainer Tom Smith. In 1938 a match race was set against the champion War Admiral, so Seabiscuit's side insisted on a start by bell. Smith got him used to leaving at the bell. When it rang, Seabiscuit lunged ahead and won. Laura Hillenbrand tells it in Seabiscuit.
key_contrast: Change the start, not the horse
